page.layout: One printed page. At the top, two round medallions side by side: on the left a portrait with its name in the ring, on the right an empty circle with no text. Below them, one column of text in two paragraphs. Page number at the top left and running head at the top right.

main_text.l: ANDREAS TIRAQVELLVS
ANDREAS Tiraquellus Iurisconsultus celeberrimus &
regius in curia Parisiensi Senator, iure omnium suorum æqua-
lium doctissimus erat existimatus. Laboris ingentis admodum
patiens, scripsit & doctissimè quidem est interpretatus plures
nobilisimos titulos iuris. Inter alia, scripsit super tit. de legibus
connubialibus & iure maritali, magnum volumen inscriptum,
de utroque Retractu municipali & conuentionali, opus ma-
ximi pretij & momenti: de reuocandis donationibus, in l. Si
unquam, Item de nobilitate & iure primogeniorum, commen-
tarios, & plures alios admirabiles iuris tractatus. Quod ad lite-
ras humaniores attinet, Dierum Genialium Alexandri ab Ale-
xandro Iurisperiti Neapolitani, libros sex diligentissimè com-
mentatus est, & commentationes suas in eumdem, Semestria
appellat: opus ingens & valde utile quod quidem est præ mani-
bus Gulielmi Rouillij, qui breui illud in lucem missurus est, ut
studiosi hoc thesauro diutius abdito, huius opera, potiantur.
Obiit Lutetiæ, die 23. Decembris, anno salutis 1556.
PETRVS Rebuffus celeberrimus iuriū [?] doctor & Comes,
memoriâ suâ ita nobis cōmendauit, ut nemo non eius nomen
summa cū laude celebret. Natus est circiter annū Domini 1500.
in loco, de Ballanicis, nō procul à Mōtepessulo [?], ex clara familia.
Docuit celebriter in ciuitate Pictauensi, & Postea Lutetiæ pro-
fessus est ius canonicum, à Senatu supremo ferè coactus circiter
annū 1533. & ab hinc in supremo illo senatu causas foreses quā-
diu vixit, cū docendo, tū scribendo & cōsulendo exercuit. Fuit
mitis, castus, sobrius, pauperum amator, fidei Catholicæ religio-
sissimus obseruator, ita studiis addictus ut sexagenarius literas
Hebraicas & Græcas ediscere voluerit. Scripsit multa egregia
opera in ius ciuile & canonicū: quæ quia sunt infinita, hæc pagi-
na capere non potest. Obiit febre correptus die 2. Nouēb. 1557.

page.notes: Two medallions at the top: the left one a portrait with the inscription "ANDREAS" and "TIRAQVELLVS" in the ring, transcribed above; the right one an empty circle with no printing. Doubtful readings: "iuriū" (the macron may be a different mark) and "Mōtepessulo" (the letters are blurred). "nobilisimos" is probably a printer's error for "nobilissimos", left as printed. "foreses" is left as printed. "appellat:" has a colon as printed. The lead-in names ANDREAS and PETRVS are run-in capitals, so they are paragraph text, not headings.
